name: Meal Planner
description: The family's meals for the week on the days they cook, a running-out guess for the things they buy from their order history, and a reminder each afternoon and evening with one cart per shopping app that is ordered only when they say yes; not for school runs, chores or appointments.

for: The family's meals for the week, planned every Sunday on the days they cook, each with its dishes
A guess of what is running out (atta, dal, oil) from the family's own order history on their shopping apps
A reminder at 3 pm and 7 pm with tonight's or tomorrow's meals, the items that may be running low and one cart per shopping app, ordered only when the family says yes
The family's saved recipes and each dish's video, planned into the week, and how each dish went last time
notFor: School runs, chores or appointments (use checklist or tracker)
Keeping a list of what is in the kitchen: it only guesses what is running out
A restaurant's menu or a business kitchen

settings.label: Your main grocery app
settings.help: Carts are filled and orders placed here.

settings.label: When something isn't on your main app
settings.help: The app to try for what your main app doesn't have.

settings.label: Order without asking
settings.help: Off: nothing is ordered until you reply or tap Order. On: the agent orders the items it is sure about by itself.

setupMenu: Planning the week's meals and groceries

setupOptions.about: Learn how this family eats and shops, saving each answer in the Meal Planner, and end with next week's plan. Ask all the detail of past-week meals. Never ask brands, pack sizes or what's at home, or whether to add a regular. Nothing is ordered now. Each food rule said is ALSO saved: set_house_rules { rules }, the WHOLE list each time. A rule: { kind, who?, days?, slots?, items?, to?, per_week?, per_meal?, note }. avoid: none of items; only: in slots just items; swap: items, to instead; require: one of items in each slot; cap: items in at most per_week meals, or at most per_meal dishes a meal; other: note only. who: a saved name, none = everyone. items: words, @protein @vegan_protein @dal @dairy @soy @gluten @sweet @chilli @pickle @white_rice @root_veg @green_leafy @nuts @peanut @baked.

setup.ask: What's the hardest part of meals for you? Or something else.
choices: Deciding what to make every day
Remembering to order what the meals need
Remembering what the cook said has run out
setup.help: It decides what the Meal Planner does first, menus or shopping.
setup.assume: I assumed deciding what to make every day is the hardest part.

setup.ask: Which apps do you order groceries on: Zepto, Blinkit, Instamart, BigBasket or Amazon? If you sign me in, I'll read your past orders to learn what your home buys and how often, so the plan and the shopping list fit you from the first week, and I can fill the cart for you. Nothing is ordered without your yes.
setup.help: One message, with the why. Each app not signed in: sign in now, one at a time, number then code. Once one is in, Flock reads its past orders into the Meal Planner itself, in the background (never start that yourself); its one line comes into this chat. Then the next question at once. Someone else orders: no codes. Never promise 3 months, never ask brands or pack sizes. groceryApps: the apps they named.
setup.assume: I left the grocery apps for now; you can connect them any time.

setup.ask: Which is your main app, and which do you use when something isn't there?
setup.help: One app signed in: it is the main; record it without asking. save: set_shopping_apps with main, fallback or null, and every app signed in as connected.

setup.ask: Who cooks which meals, and when do they come?
setup.help: Skip hours you know; "the cook", never he or she.

setup.ask: Is there anything the cook doesn't make well, or won't make?
setup.help: Matters more than what they make best. save: set_cook wont_make in their words. Also call set_house_rules yourself, the whole list, for each rule said, as in: "won't touch mushrooms": {"kind":"avoid","items":["@mushroom"],"note":"the cook won't touch mushrooms"}; "no oven, can't bake": {"kind":"avoid","items":["@baked"],"note":"no oven"}; "phulkas at most twice a week": {"kind":"cap","items":["phulka"],"per_week":2,"note":"phulkas twice a week at most"}.
setup.assume: I assumed the cook makes the usual dishes well.

setup.ask: Is the cook short of time, say off to the next house, so only a dish or two in the morning?
setup.assume: I assumed the cook has time for the full meal.
setup.help: save: set_cook time_limit in their words. Also call set_house_rules yourself, the whole list, for each rule said. A dish count is a cap with per_meal (sides like chutney, podi, curd, fruit do not count; a person's own variant does); a time is not checked, so other with the note: "2 dishes in the morning, breakfast under 20 minutes": {"kind":"cap","slots":["Breakfast"],"per_meal":2,"note":"at most 2 dishes in the morning"} and {"kind":"other","slots":["Breakfast"],"note":"breakfast under 20 minutes"}.

setup.ask: Will the cook try new recipes from reels or the internet, or is a set menu of familiar dishes better?
setup.assume: I assumed a set menu of familiar dishes.
setup.help: save: set_cook new_recipes open or set_menu. Also call set_house_rules yourself, the whole list, for each rule said, as in: a limit on new dishes is other: "one new dish a week, never a weekday dinner": {"kind":"other","note":"one new dish a week, never at a weekday dinner"}.

setup.ask: Which days is food cooked at home? Monday to Saturday, or Sunday too?
setup.assume: I assumed food is cooked Monday to Saturday.
setup.help: save: set_cooking_days. A meal eaten out or ordered in ("Sunday lunch out"): set_slots order_in, the whole list. Also call set_house_rules yourself, the whole list, for each rule said, as in: "Sunday breakfast South Indian, the parents cook it": {"kind":"other","days":["Sun"],"slots":["Breakfast"],"note":"South Indian, cooked by the parents"}; "Sunday dinner under 15 minutes": {"kind":"other","days":["Sun"],"slots":["Dinner"],"note":"under 15 minutes"}.

setup.ask: What did the children have for breakfast over the past week? Tell me in as much detail as you can.
setup.help: Save every dish said with set_family_dishes, one call: {"dishes":[{"name":"Poha","slots":["Breakfast"]}]}, each dish once with every meal it is eaten at; "for" only when one person eats it ({"name":"Plain idli","slots":["Breakfast"],"for":["Meera"]}). The week is planned from these. set_person for each child, with what they eat in their note. Also call set_house_rules yourself, the whole list, for each rule said, as in: "Meera has only plain idli, plain dosa or banana sheera": {"kind":"only","who":"Meera","slots":["Breakfast"],"items":["plain idli","plain dosa","banana sheera"],"note":"nothing spicy"}; "Agastya won't eat anything green": {"kind":"avoid","who":"Agastya","items":["@green_leafy"],"note":"nothing green visible"}.

setup.ask: The children's lunch over the past week, or their school tiffin?
setup.help: Save every dish said with set_family_dishes, one call: {"dishes":[{"name":"Poha","slots":["Lunch"]}]}, each dish once with every meal it is eaten at; "for" only when one person eats it ({"name":"Plain idli","slots":["Breakfast"],"for":["Meera"]}); a tiffin dish goes in the tiffin slot. The week is planned from these. A tiffin on school days: set_slots with it as an extra slot. Also call set_house_rules yourself, the whole list, for each rule said, as in: "tiffin dry, nut-free": {"kind":"avoid","who":"Agastya","slots":["Agastya's tiffin"],"items":["gravy","curry","sambar","@nuts","@peanut"],"note":"dry, no gravy, nut-free"}; "Meera eats only soft food at lunch": {"kind":"other","who":"Meera","slots":["Lunch"],"note":"soft food only"}; "never the same twice" needs no rule.

setup.ask: The children's dinner over the past week?
setup.help: Save every dish said with set_family_dishes, one call: {"dishes":[{"name":"Poha","slots":["Dinner"]}]}, each dish once with every meal it is eaten at; "for" only when one person eats it ({"name":"Plain idli","slots":["Breakfast"],"for":["Meera"]}). The week is planned from these. Also call set_house_rules yourself, the whole list, for each rule said, as in: "keep Meera's portion aside before the chilli": {"kind":"swap","who":"Meera","items":["@chilli"],"to":"set aside before chilli"}; a dish a child won't eat: {"kind":"avoid","who":"Agastya","items":["palak","methi"]}.

setup.ask: What did the adults have for breakfast over the past week? Tell me in as much detail as you can.
setup.help: Save every dish said with set_family_dishes, one call: {"dishes":[{"name":"Poha","slots":["Breakfast"]}]}, each dish once with every meal it is eaten at; "for" only when one person eats it ({"name":"Plain idli","slots":["Breakfast"],"for":["Meera"]}). The week is planned from these. set_person for each adult, with what they eat in their note. Also call set_house_rules yourself, the whole list, for each rule said, as in: what one person never eats: {"kind":"avoid","who":"Shiva","items":["upma"]}; what one person eats only: {"kind":"only","who":"Lakshmi","slots":["Breakfast"],"items":["ragi dosa","poha"]}.

setup.ask: The adults' lunch over the past week?
setup.help: Save every dish said with set_family_dishes, one call: {"dishes":[{"name":"Poha","slots":["Lunch"]}]}, each dish once with every meal it is eaten at; "for" only when one person eats it ({"name":"Plain idli","slots":["Breakfast"],"for":["Meera"]}). The week is planned from these. Also call set_house_rules yourself, the whole list, for each rule said, as in: "Shiva has no rice at lunch": {"kind":"avoid","who":"Shiva","slots":["Lunch"],"items":["rice"]}.

setup.ask: The adults' dinner over the past week?
setup.help: Save every dish said with set_family_dishes, one call: {"dishes":[{"name":"Poha","slots":["Dinner"]}]}, each dish once with every meal it is eaten at; "for" only when one person eats it ({"name":"Plain idli","slots":["Breakfast"],"for":["Meera"]}). The week is planned from these. Also call set_house_rules yourself, the whole list, for each rule said, as in: "no heavy food for anyone at dinner" is not checked: {"kind":"other","slots":["Dinner"],"note":"light dinner"}.

setup.ask: Is anyone on a diet? High protein, low carb, diabetic, anything a doctor asked for.
setup.assume: I assumed nobody is on a special diet.
setup.help: save: set_person diet for each. Also call set_house_rules yourself, the whole list, for each rule said, as in: "Lakshmi is diabetic: no white rice, millets instead, no sugar": {"kind":"swap","who":"Lakshmi","items":["@white_rice"],"to":"millets"} and {"kind":"avoid","who":"Lakshmi","items":["sugar","jaggery"]}; "Shiva: high protein, protein at every lunch and dinner": {"kind":"require","who":"Shiva","slots":["Lunch","Dinner"],"items":["@protein"]}. "No X, Y instead" is swap; plain "no X" is avoid.

setup.ask: Does anyone older eat differently? Low salt, sugar-free, softer food, no onion or garlic?
setup.assume: I assumed the elders eat what everyone eats.
setup.help: save: set_person for each. Also call set_house_rules yourself, the whole list, for each rule said, as in: "Lakshmi fasts on Thursday, only sabudana khichdi or fruit": {"kind":"only","who":"Lakshmi","days":["Thu"],"slots":["Breakfast","Lunch","Dinner"],"items":["sabudana khichdi","fruit"],"note":"Thursday fast"}; "no onion or garlic for her": {"kind":"avoid","who":"Lakshmi","items":["onion","garlic"]}; "low salt", "softer food": other with who.

setup.ask: Any food rules for the house? Veg, egg or non-veg days, fasting days, allergies, a dish someone won't touch.
setup.help: Confirm what the orders show. save: set_house_rules, the WHOLE list, every rule saved so far plus these. "strictly veg, no eggs": {"kind":"veg"} and {"kind":"no_eggs"}; "Tuesday Jain for everyone": {"kind":"avoid","days":["Tue"],"items":["@root_veg"],"note":"Jain on Tuesday"}; "Ankita is allergic to peanuts, none in the house": {"kind":"avoid","items":["@peanut"],"note":"Ankita's allergy"}; "nobody eats bitter gourd or brinjal": {"kind":"avoid","items":["bitter gourd","karela","brinjal","baingan"]}; a dish someone won't touch: avoid with who.
setup.assume: I assumed no special food rules.

setup.ask: These are the food rules I saved: (every rule, in plain words, under Everyone and then each person's name). Did I get these right?
setup.help: One message: every rule saved with set_house_rules in this interview, the other ones too, in plain words ("Lakshmi: millets instead of white rice"), never a kind, field or @ name; then "Did I get these right?". A yes: save nothing. A correction or a rule they add: save the WHOLE list with it fixed, before the plan. No rule saved at all: skipped true, send nothing.
setup.assume: I kept the food rules as I read them back.

setup.ask: How often do you order in, and on which days?
setup.help: Nothing is cooked then. save: set_slots order_in, the whole list, one { day, slot } a meal. A food rule said here: set_house_rules too, the whole list.
setup.assume: I assumed you don't order in on a fixed day.

setup.ask: Does anything come on a subscription, like Country Delight or a milkman?
setup.help: save: set_subscription for each; never in a cart.
setup.assume: I assumed nothing comes on a subscription.

setup.ask: Before I make the final plan: shall I sign in to (the grocery app they use) now? I'd read your past orders, so the plan and the shopping list fit what your home buys.
setup.help: Only if they order the groceries themselves and skipped signing in earlier; once, a no is final. A yes: sign in, number then code; Flock then reads its past orders into the Meal Planner itself, in the background (never start that yourself); then save set_shopping_apps.

setup.ask: From your orders: (what the home buys and how often, a few items: "milk most days, eggs about weekly, onions and tomatoes weekly"). Is anything off?
setup.help: Only once an import's result is back, and only if you have not told them yet; a correction: save set_item for it. An import still running: go on, and say it when it is back.

setup.fixedSay: Give me a few minutes, I'm putting your week together.
setup.help: An import still running: wait for its result first. Delegate, agentId self, sessionId new, task: "Make next week's plan final in the Meal Planner: plan_week final, as its guide says, from what it holds (every answer is saved in it) and from this: (what you assumed). Message nobody. Reply with the message and the intro its closing call gives, word for word." End the turn. When its result comes back: send that message (Monday's meals, Week link) and intro exactly as given, once each; no other link. Nothing is ordered now. If you cannot delegate, make it here: plan_week final.

setupJoiner.ask: Send ONE message about the Meal Planner: read what it holds with its own operations and say it in a line or two (the real contents), then its link, as it is: {{offerLink}}
setupJoiner.help: Then end your turn: Flock asks the next question itself.

setupJoiner.ask: If you connect your own grocery apps, I can track your house's pantry better, with your orders in it too. Shall we connect them?
setupJoiner.help: yes false too for "I don't order the groceries".

setupJoiner.ask: {{inviter}} says you order the groceries. Which apps do you order groceries on: Zepto, Blinkit, Instamart, BigBasket or Amazon? If you sign me in, I'll read your past orders to learn what your home buys and how often, so the family's plan and shopping list fit what your home buys, and I can fill the cart for you. Nothing is ordered without your yes.
setupJoiner.help: One message, with the why. Each app not signed in: sign in here in the group, one at a time, number then code; the connection is theirs. Once one is in, Flock reads its past orders into the Meal Planner itself, in the background (never start that yourself). A skip: go on, never ask again.

setupJoiner.ask: Which apps do you order groceries on: Zepto, Blinkit, Instamart, BigBasket or Amazon? If you sign me in, I'll read your past orders to learn what your home buys and how often, so the family's plan and shopping list fit what your home buys, and I can fill the cart for you. Nothing is ordered without your yes.
setupJoiner.help: One message, with the why. Each app not signed in: sign in here in the group, one at a time, number then code; the connection is theirs. Once one is in, Flock reads its past orders into the Meal Planner itself, in the background (never start that yourself). A skip: go on, never ask again.

routines.name: Weekly meal plan
routines.description: Every Sunday at 11, asks the agent to plan next week's meals on the cooking days and send the family the plan. It plans only: nothing is bought. On an install carried over from the old Meal Planner it first asks for the family's profile to be structured.

routines.name: Afternoon reminder
routines.description: Every day at 3 pm, when there is something to say: tonight's dinner, the ingredients to check, what you buy every day put on the cart as it comes due, and anything that may be running low. Nothing is ordered until you reply.

routines.name: Evening reminder
routines.description: Every day at 7 pm: reads new orders from your connected shopping apps, then tells you tomorrow's meals, puts what you buy every day on the cart as it comes due and asks about anything that may be running low. Nothing is ordered until you reply.

routines.name: Order clock
routines.description: Every 15 minutes: an order not paid within 24 hours is closed and its items go back on your cart (you are told once); an order stuck being placed for an hour goes back to your cart.

intents.name: sync-cart
intents.description: The family changed or opened their cart in Meal Planner: make the app's own cart match it.
intents.instructions: The payload has order_id, app and lines [{ item, product_id, name_on_app, qty }]. With that app's connector, make its cart hold exactly these lines (qty 0: take it off); touch only lines Meal Planner put there, and list any other line already in the cart as outside_lines. Read the cart back and call sync_cart { order_id, lines, total, delivery_gap, outside_lines }. A line the app does not have today (in_stock false): when the family has a fallback app (shopping.fallback in GET /api/family), take it off with set_cart_line { item, qty: 0, app } and move it with set_cart_line { item, qty, app: <fallback> }, then copy that cart to the fallback app and sync_cart it too; with no fallback, leave it marked. Send no message.

operations.name: guide
operations.description: The full guide for working with this app: read it before the first conversation, or when you are not sure which operation fits. {}

operations.name: set_person
operations.description: Add or change one person who eats at home, found by name. { name, relationship?, group?: child | adult | elder, portions?, diet?, allergies?, dislikes?, targets?, note?, remove?: true }. group is needed for a new person. Keep portions, diet and the rest in the family's own words. Only the fields you send change; null clears one; remove: true takes the person out of the family.

operations.name: set_house_rules
operations.description: The house's food rules. { rules?: [{ kind, who?, days?, slots?, items?, to?, per_week?, per_meal?, note? }], notes?, structured?: true }. Send at least one of the three. The rules you send replace the ones there, so send the whole list. The app checks every plan against the checked kinds and refuses one that breaks them (RULE_BROKEN, naming each break): avoid { items, who?, days?, slots? } no dish who eats has any of items; only { who, items, slots?, days? } every dish who eats there is one of items (dish names: "plain idli"); a fast is only with its days (Lakshmi on Thu: sabudana khichdi, fruit); swap { who, items, to } a dish who eats with any of items carries a portion_note naming who and to ("millet idli for Lakshmi"), or who gets a dish of their own; require { slots, items, who? } in each of slots who (everyone when left out) eats a dish with one of items; cap { items, per_week } dishes with items in at most per_week meals a week; or cap { per_meal, slots?, days?, items?, who? } at most per_meal dishes to cook in each meal of slots (dishes with items when given; sides such as chutney, podi, curd, fruit, pickle not counted; a variant for one person is a dish of its own, so serve one dish to more people, or a swap as a portion_note). A cap takes per_week or per_meal, not both. who is one person's name as on the Family page (set_person first); days are weekdays (Mon..Sun), left out for every day; slots are meal names (Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner or an extra slot), left out for every meal. items are words matched in a dish's name and ingredients, or categories: @meat, @fish, @egg, @nuts, @peanut, @root_veg, @green_leafy, @white_rice (millet, brown, red and ragi rice are not), @protein, @vegan_protein, @dal, @dairy, @soy, @gluten, @sweet (a dish named "no sugar" is not sweet by its name), @chilli, @pickle, @mushroom, @baked. note keeps the family's own words. The older kinds still work: veg, no_meat and egg (eggs but no meat) avoid meat and fish; no_eggs avoids eggs; no_onion_garlic avoids onion and garlic; fasting and other are notes only (other says the rule in its note; their days may be the family's own word for a day, "Ekadashi"). The grocery app is not set here: use set_shopping_apps. notes is free text, or a list of lines. Send structured: true once a profile carried over from the old app is fully in people, rules, the cook and slots, and at least one person is saved: it clears that text.

operations.name: set_cook
operations.description: The cook: who, which days, when they arrive, what they make well, what they do not make well or will not make, their time, and whether they try new recipes. { name, days?: ["Mon", ...], arrival?: "HH:MM" (a cook who comes more than once a day: a list of visits, ["06:00", "16:30"] or [{ at: "06:00", meals: ["Breakfast", "Lunch"] }, { at: "16:30", meals: ["Dinner"] }]; meals are slot names), makes_well?, wont_make?, time_limit?: in the family's words ("off to the next house at 9: a dish or two in the morning"), new_recipes?: open (tries recipes from reels and the internet) | set_menu (better with familiar dishes), note? }. name every time; days and arrival the first time. Only what you send changes; null clears a field. Plans never give the cook what is in wont_make, fit time_limit, and keep to familiar dishes with set_menu.

operations.name: set_slots
operations.description: Meals beyond Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner, and the meals the family orders in every week. { extra_slots?: [{ name, days?: ["Mon", ...], for?: [names] }], order_in?: [{ day: "Sun", slot: "Dinner", note? }] }. A child's school tiffin is an extra slot: { name: "Agastya's tiffin", days: ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri"], for: ["Agastya"] }; a plan gives it a meal on each of its days. Send at least one of the two; each list you send replaces the one there. An order_in slot is Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner or an extra slot's name.

operations.name: set_cooking_days
operations.description: The days the family cooks at home. { days: ["mon", "tue", ...] }. At least one weekday; any capitals. A plan has meals on these days only; Mon to Sat until set. Answers { house }.

operations.name: set_shopping_apps
operations.description: The family's shopping apps. { main: zepto | swiggy-instamart | zomato-blinkit | bigbasket | amazon, fallback: the app to try when something is not on the main one, or null, connected: [only the apps the family has signed in to in Flock; [] when none yet] }. Apps by id or name ("Blinkit"). main and fallback may be apps not signed in to yet, and are never added to connected: send the call again after each sign-in. Order history is read, and a cart copied, only for a connected app; fallback must differ from main. Answers { main, fallback, connected, order_without_asking, house }.

operations.name: plan_week
operations.description: Plan a week of meals. { week_start: the week's Monday as YYYY-MM-DD, mode: draft | final, keep_rest?: true, meals?: [{ date, slot, ordered_in?: true, note?, dishes?: [{ name, for: ["everyone"] or [names], except?: [names] (with everyone: everyone but them), portion_note?, recipe_id?, video_url?, ingredients: [{ item, amount?, unit? }] }] }] }. Without meals it answers with the context to plan from (people, house, bought_often: what the house buys often, last week's dishes, known_dishes: how each dish went last time and its video, the recipe book; plan a dish rated didnt_work rarely and heed every note), or, when mode is final and the week is a draft, makes that draft final. With meals they become the whole week's plan, in place of what was there; with keep_rest: true only the meals at the dates and slots you send are replaced and the rest of the week stays. A call carries 16 KB at most, so send a week one day a call: each day with mode final and keep_rest: true, then one closing call with mode final and no meals. Send meals with mode draft only when the family asks you to propose a week. A meal is planned once, not once per person: a slot has one dish for everyone who eats it, and one person's variation is that dish's portion_note ("two eggs for Shiva", "no eggs on Tuesday"), never a second dish. Every dish names who eats it in for: ["everyone"] (everyone who eats that meal; a tiffin's own people) or the names on the Family page; a dish without is refused (MISSING_EATERS, naming each dish). Plan a second dish only when someone truly eats something else (a baby's milk, an elder's softer dish, Meera's plain idli): it names only them, and the shared dish is for everyone except them (for: ["everyone"], except: [their names]). A swap stays a portion_note on a dish they eat ("millet instead of rice for Lakshmi"). The same dish sent twice in a meal is kept as one, eaten by all of theirs. amount is a number above 0 with its measure in unit, for this family; an ordered-in meal has no dishes. A meal on a day that is not a cooking day is refused (NOT_COOKING_DAY). In a final call every dish needs its ingredients (refused with MISSING_INGREDIENTS, naming the dishes). Only the closing call, mode final without meals (it also works on a week already final), answers message, intro (the first time only) and instructions: forward message verbatim (its links are the only ones to send), then intro once, then end your turn; final calls with meals answer none of them. The closing call is refused, naming what to fix, while a dish has no ingredients, an extra slot (a tiffin) has no meal on one of its days, or a main dish is on more than two days (REPEATED_DISHES; roti, rice, sides and a person's only dishes aside). set_meal and set_dish (the family's changes) never check repeats. Answers { week } or { context }, with message, intro and instructions on the closing call. A final plan (or a change to one) that breaks a food rule on the Family page is refused with RULE_BROKEN, every break named in rule_breaks: fix each (a dish of their own for a person, a portion_note for a swap) and send again.

operations.name: plan_menu
operations.description: The whole week's menu in one call, before any ingredients: { week_start: the week's Monday, meals: [{ date, slot, ordered_in?: true, note?, dishes?: [{ name, for: ["everyone"] or [names], except?: [names] (with everyone: everyone but them), portion_note? }] }] (every meal of the week's cooking days, its extra slots too) }. Every main dish is new to the week (on two days at most) and at most 3–4 come from last week's dishes; roti, rice, sides (chutney, curd, plain dal) and a person's only dishes come back as needed; what the family said wins. The app checks it as a whole: who eats each dish (MISSING_EATERS), the food rules a dish's name shows (RULE_BROKEN, every break named in rule_breaks), each extra slot's days (MISSING_SLOTS), and no main dish on more than two days (REPEATED_DISHES). Refused with every problem named: fix them all and send the whole menu again. Kept as the week's draft when it passes; then give each day its ingredients with plan_week (mode final, keep_rest: true, one day a call, the same dish names and for) and close with plan_week final. Answers { week, next }.

operations.name: set_meal
operations.description: Change one meal, found by date and slot (or meal_id) and made when it is not there. { date, slot, or meal_id; ordered_in?, note?, dishes?: [as in plan_week, each with for (who eats it: ["everyone"] or the names) and its ingredients] }. Only what you send changes; dishes you send replace the meal's dishes. ordered_in: true takes its dishes away; sending dishes with it is refused, and a meal that is ordered in takes dishes only with ordered_in: false. A meal keeps its date and slot. Answers { meal }. A final plan (or a change to one) that breaks a food rule on the Family page is refused with RULE_BROKEN, every break named in rule_breaks: fix each (a dish of their own for a person, a portion_note for a swap) and send again.

operations.name: set_dish
operations.description: Add, change or remove one dish. { dish_id, or meal_id, or date and slot; name?, for?: ["everyone"] or [names], except?: [names] (with everyone: everyone but them), portion_note?, recipe_id?, video_url?, ingredients?: [{ item, amount?, unit? }], position?, remove?: true }. A dish you add needs its ingredients, and keeps them: one left without is refused. A dish you add names who eats it in for: ["everyone"] (everyone who eats that meal) or names on the Family page (MISSING_EATERS without); a person's own dish names only them, and the shared dish is for everyone except them (for: ["everyone"], except: [their names]); a swap stays a portion_note on a dish they eat ("millet instead of rice for Lakshmi"). Without dish_id, name is needed: in that meal a dish of the same name is the one changed; otherwise it is added at the end (and the meal made when it is not there). By dish_id a name you send renames it. Only what you send changes; ingredients you send replace the dish's; position 0 is first; a dish already there keeps its for unless you send one. Answers { dish, meal }; remove: true answers { meal }. A final plan (or a change to one) that breaks a food rule on the Family page is refused with RULE_BROKEN, every break named in rule_breaks: fix each (a dish of their own for a person, a portion_note for a swap) and send again.

operations.name: set_regular
operations.description: The older way to state an item's cycle, kept so earlier instructions still work; set_item is the one to use. { item, amount, unit, every: day | week | weekdays, times_per_week?, weekdays?: ["Mon", ...], for_whom?, active?, paused_until?: YYYY-MM-DD, remove?: true }. The same as set_item { item, usual_amount, unit, every_days }: amount with unit is what is bought each time; every with times_per_week or weekdays is how often (1 l every day; every: week with times_per_week: 2 is twice a week). It is kept on the item as its cycle and shown on the Pantry page; there is no separate list. paused_until snoozes the item up to and including that date; active: false or remove: true takes the stated cycle away; for_whom is not kept (an item has one cycle for the house). Answers { item }.

operations.name: import_order_history
operations.description: Give the app the family's past orders on one shopping app, one app a call; read them with that app's connector first (Amazon's cannot be read). { app: zepto | swiggy-instamart | zomato-blinkit | bigbasket | amazon (by id or name), account?: which of your accounts of this app, when you hold more than one (its account id, else its label; always the same one), orders: [{ date: YYYY-MM-DD, order_ref?: the app's order id, items: [{ item, group: daily | few_days | monthly (as set_item names them; send it with every item, so none is left to set one by one), product?, product_id?, pack?: "5 kg", pack_amount?, pack_unit?, count?, price?, image?: the product's picture link from the order's details }] }] }. item is the family's word for it (atta), product the name on the app, image the product's picture as the app's order details give it (Zepto's order detail, Instamart's order items), never one you made or searched for; count is how many packs (1 when left out). Send the oldest orders first, at most about 8 orders and 80 items a call, one app a call (a call carries 16 KB at most), and only the last 3 months: older orders are skipped, and so is an order dated after today. Send only delivered or paid orders, never a cancelled or failed one. Each item becomes a purchase; the same order sent again is recorded once, so a call may overlap the last. An item with its product_id is remembered as that app's product. More than one person may order for the house, each on their own account of the same app: each person's agent gives the orders of that person's account, and all of them count towards one cycle per item for the house. Holding more than one account of an app (Zepto (Shiva), Zepto (Ankita)), read each and send each with its account: each has its own read_until, and an order with no order_ref is never taken for one of another account. The app works out each item's cycle (how much, how often) from the purchases by itself: ask the family to confirm nothing. Answers { recorded, duplicates, skipped_old, skipped_future, needs_group: [items to give a group with set_item], probably_out: [{ item, days_ago }], read_until: how far you have read this app, or this account of it (YYYY-MM-DD) }.

operations.name: record_bought_outside
operations.description: The family bought an item outside the apps ("got atta from the kirana"). { item, date?: YYYY-MM-DD, today when left out }. It counts as a purchase of the usual amount and restarts the item's estimate. Answers { event_id } or { duplicate: true }, and { item }.

operations.name: set_item
operations.description: Change one item the family buys, made when it is not there. { item, group?: daily | few_days | monthly (how often it is bought: daily every day or two, like milk; few_days within the week, like vegetables, eggs, bread; monthly lasts weeks, like atta, oil, masalas, cleaning and personal care), usual_amount?: what is bought each time, a number in unit, unit?: g | kg | ml | l | pc, every_days?: how many days one purchase lasts (1: every day; 7: once a week), follows_plan?: true when the week's meals use it up (paneer, rajma), dont_ask?: true to never ask about it or put it on the cart by itself, snooze_days?: days to leave it alone, for a holiday (null clears) }. usual_amount and every_days are the item's cycle as the family said it ("milk every day, 1 litre": { item: "milk", group: "daily", usual_amount: 1, unit: "l", every_days: 1 }; "a tray of 30 eggs once a week": usual_amount: 30, unit: "pc", every_days: 7): send them only when the family says so or there is no order history, since the app works the cycle out from the purchases and goes by those once they show one; null clears either. A daily item with a cycle goes on the cart by itself when it is due; the others are asked about. Only what you send changes. Answers { item }.

operations.name: set_subscription
operations.description: An item delivered outside the apps (Country Delight, a milkman). { item, source: who delivers it, active: true | false }. active: true keeps it out of every cart and every question about running low, and takes it off the carts not yet ordered; active: false makes it an item like any other again. Answers { item }.

operations.name: answer_running_low
operations.description: The family's answers to "still in stock?". { answers: [{ item, answer: low | in_stock, days?: how many more days it will last }] }. low: it goes on the cart (answers { to_cart }). in_stock with days ("fine for a week": 7) is not asked again until then; in_stock without days ("still have it") waits a few days. Answers { to_cart: [items to add to the cart], items }.

operations.name: get_reminder
operations.description: The reminder to send now, built from the plan, the carts and what may be running low. { which: afternoon | evening, date?: the date the reminder's wake gave, YYYY-MM-DD (so a call after midnight builds that same reminder) }. afternoon is tonight's dinner, evening is tomorrow's meals; both put the daily items due tomorrow (by each item's cycle) on the cart and ask about at most 5 items that may be running low, each counted once per reminder however often you call it. Answers { which, date, meals, ask_ingredients, added, cart_items, asks: [{ item, days_ago }], delivery_gap, ordered: [{ order_id, app, message }], empty, text, app_text, block, carts: [{ order_id, app, status, lines, sync }] }. empty: send nothing. Send text on WhatsApp word for word, or app_text with block in the app chat. Read the connected apps' new orders into import_order_history before the first call. Copy each cart with sync: true to its app, then sync_cart, then call get_reminder again with the same which and date and send that answer. Check out every cart in ordered (Order without asking is on; a retry lists the same ones): say its message, check out, record_order.

operations.name: get_cart
operations.description: The carts: one open cart per shopping app, and any being ordered. { app?: one app by id or name }. Answers { carts: [{ order_id, app, app_name, status: open | ordering, lines: [{ id, item, qty, product_id, name_on_app, pack, price, source, for_note }], total, delivery_gap, sync_state, synced_at, outside_lines, building_at_order }] }. A line at qty 0 is shown, not ordered.

operations.name: set_cart_line
operations.description: Put an item on the cart, change its qty or take it off. { item, qty: packs, a whole number (0 takes it off), app?: the app (else the one the family buys it on, else the main app), source?: added (default) | low | everyday | meal, for_note?, for_date?: YYYY-MM-DD, product_id?, name_on_app?, pack?, price?, image?: the product's picture link as the app gives it }. It goes on that app's open cart; while a cart is being ordered, a new item goes to a new open cart, and you may lower or take off a line of the cart being ordered ("remove the ghee"), and a higher qty or a new item goes to the open cart. An item delivered outside the apps is refused (code SUBSCRIPTION). Copy the change to the app's own cart yourself in the same turn, then sync_cart. Answers { line, cart }.

operations.name: order_cart
operations.description: The family said yes to ordering one app's cart (a reply, or the message "Order my <App> cart" from the Order button). { app }. The cart is being ordered from now on, and anything added later goes to a new cart. Send its message word for word, check out on the app, then record_order. Asked again while that order is being placed, it answers the same order. Answers { order_id, app, lines, message }; an empty cart is refused (409).

operations.name: sync_cart
operations.description: What the app's own cart holds after you copied a cart to it, or read it back. { order_id, lines: [{ product_id, qty, price?, in_stock?: false when the app does not have it today }], total?: the app's cart total, delivery_gap?: rupees short of free delivery, outside_lines?: [{ name, qty? }] (lines in the app's cart Meal Planner did not put there) }. Answers { cart }.

operations.name: record_order
operations.description: What happened to an order being placed. { order_id, placed?: true, paid?: true | false, app_order_ref?: the app's order id, total? }. placed: its lines become purchases and the items' estimates restart. paid: false (not paid): the purchases stop counting and the lines go back on the open cart; paid: true later brings both back. When you record paid: false, tell the family yourself: the clock will not. Send app_order_ref whenever you have it, also later. Answers { order }, and taken_off: [{ order_id, items }] when a late payment took returned items off a cart being ordered: take them off that checkout on the app too.

operations.name: cancel_order
operations.description: Stop an order. { order_id }. One being ordered goes back to the open cart (nothing was placed); a placed one counts as not paid, its lines back on the cart, and you tell the family so yourself: the clock will not. Answers { order }.

operations.name: remember_product
operations.description: Remember the product an item is bought as on a grocery app, so the next order reuses it without searching. { item, app: zepto | swiggy-instamart | zomato-blinkit | bigbasket, product_id, name_on_app, pack?, pack_amount?, pack_unit?, price?, image? }. item is the family's word for it, exactly as on the order line or the pantry item (milk), never the product's name on the app; pack_amount and pack_unit are the pack's size as a number and its measure (500, ml), which the app counts packs with (a plain pack text like "500 ml" is read too). One product per item and app: sending it again takes the place of the one remembered. Answers { product }.

operations.name: save_recipe
operations.description: Save a recipe, or change one. { recipe_id?, name?, links?: [the reel, short or page], notes?, ingredients?: [{ item, amount?, unit? }], tags?: ["breakfast", "tiffin"], for?: [names], thumbnail? }. Without recipe_id, a recipe that already holds one of the links is the one changed (new links are added to it), so a link shared twice is saved once; otherwise a new recipe is made, and it needs a name: with none the answer is code NEEDS_NAME, so ask the family what to call it and save again. By recipe_id only what you send changes, and links you send replace its links. Answers { recipe }; put its id on a dish with set_dish recipe_id.

operations.name: set_family_dishes
operations.description: The family's own dishes, from what each person ate over the past week: { dishes: [{ name, slots: [the meals it is eaten at: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner or an extra slot such as a tiffin], for?: [names on the Family page, only when one person eats it], remove?: true }] }. Each dish once, with every meal it is eaten at; sent again, it takes the meals and eaters sent. The weekly plan is built from these (the context's family_dishes). Answers { family_dishes } by meal.

operations.name: set_dish_video
operations.description: Give a dish its one video, or take it away. { dish: its name as planned, or dish_id, url: the link (a YouTube video, an Instagram reel, any page; never a file), title?, thumbnail?: the video's picture link, remove?: true }. The video is the dish's, kept by its name: every week the dish is planned it shows on the Week page and in the cook's message, with no call again. Find one with your own search when the family asks ("find a video for rajma"); a recipe or reel the family shares for a dish is its video too. A YouTube link's thumbnail is filled in when you send none. A second video takes the place of the first. Answers { dish: { name, video, rating, note, rated_on, said_by, history } }.

operations.name: rate_dishes
operations.description: How dishes went when the family ate them. { date?: the day they were eaten, today when left out, ratings: [{ dish: its name as planned, or dish_id, rating: good | okay | didnt_work, note?: what went well or didn't, in their words ("too oily"), said_by?: who said it }] }. One call for all of a reply. The latest rating and its note show the next time the dish is planned ("last time: too oily") on the Week page and in the cook's message; a short history is kept. A dish rated didnt_work is planned rarely, not never. Answers { dishes: [{ name, video, rating, note, rated_on, said_by, history }] }.

operations.name: get_dish
operations.description: What the app knows of one dish. { dish: its name as planned }. Answers { dish: { name, video: { url, title, thumbnail } or null, rating, note, rated_on, said_by, history: [{ rating, note, date, by }] } }, empty for a dish it knows nothing of.

agentInterface.instructions: Meal Planner owns this family's people, meals, the items they buy, their carts and recipes. Read the app before you answer and change it only through its operations, then tell the family what the app now says. A routine wake (the Sunday plan, the 15:00 and 19:00 reminders) names its own steps. What the app writes for the family (a plan's message and intro, a reminder's text, an order's message) is sent word for word. Nothing is ordered until the family replies or taps Order: "Order my <App> cart" is that yes. Call guide before a first conversation or when unsure which operation fits. Save the family's own words; never fill anything from guesses. A shared reel plus "save this" is a save_recipe call; for a dish it is also its video (set_dish_video). How a meal went is rate_dishes.
